page: Amazon Web Services m8ib.large is an entry-tier general-purpose instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features a dedicated x86_64 Intel processor operating at a clock speed of 3.9 GHz. Compute resources comprise two virtual CPUs derived from a single physical core with two execution threads per core. System memory totals 8.0 GB of RAM, establishing a standard 1:4 core-to-memory allocation ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. No hardware accelerators or dedicated GPUs are bundled with this configuration.

Network connectivity provides a baseline bandwidth of 2 Gbps, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned by default. The instance includes no local NVMe storage, meaning all persistent file systems and boot volumes must be attached via remote block storage networks. Because storage is decoupled, input and output performance is directly tied to network storage bandwidth rather than on-host drives.

This server type is engineered for lightweight production services, microservices, small web servers, staging environments, and intermediate caching layers that require stable CPU clock performance with modest memory requirements.
description: Amazon Web Services m8ib.large is an x86_64 general-purpose instance based on the AWS Nitro hypervisor platform. It is equipped with two dedicated vCPUs sourced from a single Intel physical core running at 3.9 GHz, paired with 8.0 GB of system memory, matching a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory configuration. The server contains no local storage and no GPU accelerators, necessitating network-attached block storage for persistent volumes. Baseline network throughput is provisioned at 2 Gbps without complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Given its dedicated single-core compute profile, standard memory balance, and network-dependent disk architecture, the m8ib.large is designed for moderate utility workloads, container hosting, API backends, development environments, and small-scale transactional web services.
